title: A system-centered probabilistic formalism linking multiple equilibria and biodiversity in ecological and evolutionary models
summary: Ecological and evolutionary communities do not always settle into a single predictable configuration. Models such as Lotka-Volterra or replicator dynamics may predict several admissible states. The multiplicity of such states is central to understanding robustness, alternative community configurations, coexistence, and shifts in biodiversity. Yet, standard practices are often state-centered: they either focus on the properties of typical equilibria or pool states across systems, losing information about how many states can arise in a single system, including cases where no state exists.…
